intended_object: The barycentric (homogeneous) coordinate functions t_0, …, t_n of the algebraic n-simplex Δⁿ_R = R[t_0,…,t_n]/(t_0+⋯+t_n − 1). Here this ring is presented as the polynomial ring R[t_1,…,t_n] with central variables, so t_0 = 1 − (t_1+⋯+t_n). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: `PolyRing R n` is the monoid algebra R[ℕ^(Fin n)], i.e. polynomials in n central variables over an arbitrary unital ring R. `generator n j` is the variable t_{j+1}. The definition sends index 0 to 1 − Σ_j t_j and index j+1 to t_{j+1}. This is exactly the standard identification of R[t_0,…,t_n]/(Σ t_i − 1) with R[t_1,…,t_n], in which t_0 is eliminated using the relation Σ t_i = 1. The construction already works over any unital ring, possibly noncommutative, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no algebraic simplex or barycentric coordinates in this form: its `MvPolynomial` needs a commutative coefficient ring, and the library deliberately uses `AddMonoidAlgebra` to handle noncommutative R. The definition matches the intended object, so the verdict is faithful.
